Wild shelters
Yukkuri occupy existing caves or pits and bring loose leaves and bedding. Capacity follows usable ground.
A few twigs form their so-called boundary; they build no walls or roof and gain no defense.

Open pits allow sleep in dry weather; rain forces a search for real cover.

notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.start:
Field notebook

Use in the air for this guide. Use on a yukkuri to read its current state and record its species.

Observing does not feed, heal or change personality.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.route:
First supplies

Book + feather: notebook.
Chest + 2 string: carrier.
Bowl + 2 clay balls: food bowl.
Hay bale + white wool + string: nest.
3 oak planks + sand: potty.
Build a roof and clear entrance first.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.discovery:
Discovery and transport

Explore plains, forests and meadows. Look for families and shelters.
Use a carrier on a living yukkuri, then on dry supported ground. Blocked space or water prevents release; the carrier stays full.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.care:
Food and cleaning

Put apples, bread or oil grain in a bowl. Food provides nutrition only after swallowing.
Wet a cloth at a water source. Use it to clean the potty. Food, waste and cleaning all use real items.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.water:
Water and medicine

Offer water potions or yogurt for dryness, constipation or spicy food. Oral effects begin at swallowing.
Sleep spray has a delay. Stimulant adds drive; baby-talk medicine changes speech, not body age.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.social:
Familiarity

Empty-hand use speaks gently. Sneak-use opens the care menu, including colder replies. Teach with a whistle; introduce adults with a cord.
The needs page shows affection, boredom and activities. Danger interrupts care.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.home:
A place to rest

Use the notebook on a nest or shelter to select it, then sneak-use on a yukkuri to assign it. A real entrance and standing space are required.
Twig boundaries do not block rain or enemies.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.family:
Family and growth

Healthy familiar adults need nearby homes, food and rest. Pairing does not guarantee pregnancy; population and sleeping space also matter.
Ancestry records actual parents. Young grow with nourishment and rest.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.birth:
Birth

Standard kinds can bear stems. Apply reproductive filling continuously to an eligible adult for assisted live pregnancy; the father is unknown.
The brood page shows progress. House kinds lay eggs. Detached broods stay in the world.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.house:
House kinds

Place a house crevice under shelter with a clear entrance. Provide scraps, paper, string or wheat for carrying and nesting.
Eggs need food and care. Sneak-cleaning a nest affects eggs and lining; inspect it first.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.body:
Body condition

Check wounds, infection, filling and mold. Orange juice and mold remover have different uses.
A short wash differs from prolonged rain or immersion. Food lures do not make ordinary kinds safe river swimmers.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.tools:
Tools and interruption

Tools affect real body parts or held items. Follow the operation menu for the target and action.
Distance, danger or movement can interrupt continuous work. Check the item and condition before trying again.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.play:
Play and surroundings

Offer yarn, marbles, balls or dolls. Tunnels, slides and trampolines need reachable entrances and landings.
Lining changes surface contact; sandpaper abrades. Pools still cause wetness and immersion.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.storage:
Cold storage

Craft with 4 iron ingots, 2 snow blocks, a chest, redstone and an ender pearl.
Use a full carrier on it. All cabinets share four places per player. Age, physiology and internal pregnancy pause without cold damage.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.retrieval:
Retrieving

Use an empty carrier to take the oldest occupant, then release on dry ground. Empty-hand use lists the vault.
Breaking a cabinet does not delete occupants. Rebuild to recover them, including after death or travel.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.commerce:
Human facilities

Look for caretakers, shops and factories near settlements. Their menus show current stock and conditions.
Animals retain their identity in trade. Factory work requires real parents, supplies and routes.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.progress:
Survival progress

Get a notebook, observe and assign a home. Also prepare care supplies, store and retrieve an occupant, and raise a real family.
Successful events record once. There are no item or XP rewards to farm.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.status:
Content status

Species pages use the current registry; only actual observation marks discovery.
Predators and new forms have separate acceptance checks. Registration is not full validation. Optional guide/HUD integrations are absent.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.standard_spec:
Standard living kind. Observe the individual for age, personality, family, body and consumable state.
A species name is not a health or intelligence rating.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.house_species:
House ecology. These kinds collect scraps, carry nesting supplies and reproduce through nest eggs.
An ordinary yukkuri does not become a house kind merely by going indoors.
notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.predator:
Predator kind. Plan separate space from ordinary pets. Flight, hunting, nests and trade are under separate implementation checks.
This registry entry does not certify every behavior.

notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.aquatic:
Aquatic Marisa

Her body still fears water; her own large hat is her floating home. Right-click with a stick to give a paddle. Sneak-click an adult at a bank to launch; repeating this on the captain capsizes her boat.

Give food to the hat to store it (sneak: up to 8 portions); empty-hand click from dry ground to rescue.

Forages, cares for young and sleeps afloat. Shore visits are brief: toilet needs, supplies or emergencies. Her delicate soles cannot tolerate long land stays or inland wandering.

notebook.mcyukkuri.chapter.aquatic_famil:
Family life afloat

Wait for all the young before leaving shore. Spend the day afloat and sleep in the hat at night.

Small juveniles stand on supported brim spaces; others and babies rest inside. Once large enough, a pupil lowers its own hat from its father's boat and practices a short round trip. The father holds position and keeps its return berth free.

Giving a stick to a young passenger equips that child. Sneak-giving requests a first voyage. Parents serve real food, nuzzle their young and hum before sleep.

Birth and growth

A parent approaches and lowers its head to pass real mash through mouth contact. The first bowel movement needs nearby parental care. Safe crawling and actual takeoff and landing practice develop movement.
